newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-EXPRESS THROUGH TO FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EXPRESS THROUGH TO FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Ugandan club Express FC, semifinalists in the African Champions Cup two years ago, overcame the ignomy of having to play in this year's preliminary round by beating Young Africans from neighbouring Tanzania and qualifyig for the first round.
Express, unusually included in the preliminaries of Africa's top club competition despite their achievement in 1995, beat Young Africans 1-0 in Kampala on Saturday to win by a single aggregate goal.
The match was one of 12 preliminary round second leg matches played in the three African club competitions at the weekend.
Suleiman Tenywa kept up his impressive knack of scoring vital goals to give the Ugandans a 1-0 aggregate win in this tense east African derby.
Tenywa also scored the winner in December's East and Central African Challenge Cup final in which Uganda beat their Sudanese hosts.
Express now play Zimbabwe's Caps United in the first round next month.
They are joined in the round of 32 by Congo's Munisport, Junior Professionals of Liberia, Cape Verdians Desportivo Travadores, FC BFV of Madagascar and Lesotho's representatives Roma Rovers.
Rovers scored a shock 5-1 home win over Limbe Leaf Wanderers in Maseru on Sunday to set up a lucrative meeting with Orlando Pirates from neighbouring South Africa. Rovers won 5-2 on aggregate.
Desportivo Travadores from the tiny island group of the Cape Verde provided another upset with a 2-1 aggregate win over Mogas 90 of Benin.
The Cape Verdians won Sunday's second leg 2-0 at home with goals from Lemos and Tazinho.
Junior Professionals, the Liberian club who are bankrolled by AC Milan's George Weah, played an astute defensive game against Racing Club Bobo-Dialassou in Ouagadougou on Sunday.
The Liberians led 2-0 from the first leg in Monrovia two weeks ago and kept out their opposition until four minutes from the end of Sunday's second leg.
But Temani Traore's 86th minute goal was not enough for Racing Club, who went down 2-1 on aggregate.

In the African Cup Winners' Cup, Chad's Renaissance scored a first-ever away win in African club competition to beat Akonangui of Equatorial Guinea 4-1 in Bata on Sunday and go through 7-1 on aggregate.
The Chadians' last appearance in the Cup Winners' Cup saw them lose by a record 13-0 to Mbilinga of Gabon three years ago.
Also through to the first round are Eleven Men in Flight from Swaziland, Lesotho's Lerotholi Polytechnic, Bata Bullets of Malawi and Uganda's Umeme FC and Zimbabwe's glamour club Dynamos.
Dynamos overcame a one-goal deficit against Sigara of Tanzania to win 3-0 in Harare on Sunday with goals from internationals Ian Gorowa, Memory Mucherahowa and Lloyd Mutasa.

Tanzania's surviving representative in African competition this year remains Simba of Dar-es-Salaam, who won through to the first round of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup with a 5-1 aggregate win over Dire Dawa Locomotive FC of Ethiopi.
A 1-0 away win in Addis Ababa on Sunday gave Simba an easy passage and they now have a derby encounter with AFC Leopards of Kenya in the first round next month.
